scenarios.title: An invalidation retires the old reader
scenarios.description: One product changes from v41 / INR 499.00 to v42 / INR 549.00. Watch the ticket generation, source floor and fill result.

steps.title: Reader A gets a ticket before reading v41
steps.note: The origin fixture supplies v41 at INR 499.00. The cache has no value yet, but it has a bounded metadata slot and a ticket issued at t=0.

steps.title: The committed v42 invalidation arrives
steps.note: The slot's generation advances and its version floor becomes 42. An invalidation retires pending work as well as removing old bytes.

steps.title: The delayed v41 fill is rejected
steps.note: Reader A's ticket names generation 0 while the slot now has generation 1. The cache stays empty; the old price cannot refill it with this ticket.

steps.title: A new ticket fills the current version
steps.note: A fresh authoritative fixture supplies v42 at INR 549.00. It meets the retained floor and generation. This ticket starts its own ten-second budget at t=2.

steps.title: An older invalidation is harmless
steps.note: Version 41 is below the retained floor 42, so the event cannot lower the floor or delete the newer value.

scenarios.title: A delayed fill does not get a new TTL
scenarios.description: The hard age starts before reading the origin and survives the fill. This is independent of invalidation delivery.

steps.title: The load starts at t=0
steps.note: No invalidation arrives in this case. The separate age budget must stop a delayed origin snapshot from being renewed indefinitely.

steps.title: At t=9, a late fill has one second left
steps.note: The cache stores the original ticket start, not the fill time. remainingMillis is 1000, so this cannot become a new ten-second copy.

steps.title: Just before the deadline
steps.note: The original permission has one millisecond left in this controlled ticker scenario. A read does not reset it.

steps.title: Equality ends the permission
steps.note: At t=10, age equals the ten-second limit. get removes the value and returns a miss. Retained metadata still carries its version floor.

steps.title: The same old ticket cannot renew it
steps.note: fill rejects the exhausted ticket. A new ticket and a new authoritative read are needed; reinserting the old bytes is insufficient.

scenarios.title: Eviction retires both data and old permission
scenarios.description: Use tiny capacities to see exact LRU, the separate byte bound, and why a recreated key needs a new slot incarnation.

steps.title: Two slots and six payload bytes are full
steps.note: Slot order is least-recent to most-recent. Tickets can remain in flight, but cache-owned metadata itself is bounded.

steps.title: Reading A changes recency, not age
steps.note: B is now least recent. A's remaining budget still comes from its original ticket; a hit does not refresh its TTL.

steps.title: Loading C evicts B's entire slot
steps.note: The slot count stays at two and payload stays at six bytes. B's old slot identity is retired, including its generation history.

steps.title: Four bytes for A require C to leave
steps.note: Slot capacity alone is insufficient when values grow. The encoded-payload budget evicts C before accepting the larger A.

steps.title: Recreating A does not revive its old ticket
steps.note: A is now slot 4, while the old ticket still names slot 1. Matching key text and generation zero do not restore old permission.
